answer: One anti-sybil mechanism: decisions need a stake-weighted quorum from provably independent validators. A proposal passes only when enough staked weight approves AND that weight spans many uncorrelated sources, not one cluster. Picture each validator as a thread; a vote holds only if the threads form a diverse weave, not one spool. A thousand correlated fakes buy no quorum, counting as a single source, so the network is no haven for one actor in many masks. To sway a vote an attacker needs genuinely independent stake, real separately-held capital, not a mass-minted sonnet of shells.
